skipped_properties.reason: exploitability: configuration-error (requires node restart with lost persistence)

checklist.title: Falsify constant gas charge for secp256r1 precompile across all input paths
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Deploy a contract that calls the secp256r1 precompile (address 0x100) with various inputs: (a) valid 160-byte input with correct signature, (b) valid 160-byte input with invalid signature, (c) empty input (0 bytes), (d) input shorter than 160 bytes, (e) input longer than 160 bytes. 2. For each call, measure exact gas consumed using gasleft() before and after the STATICCALL. 3. Verify that in ALL cases, exactly 6900 gas is deducted. 4. If any input path consumes different gas, the invariant is violated - attacker can spam cheap calls.
executable_checks: Assert gasBefore - gasAfter == 6900 for valid signature verification
Assert gasBefore - gasAfter == 6900 for invalid signature (wrong r,s values)
Assert gasBefore - gasAfter == 6900 for malformed input (< 160 bytes)
Assert gasBefore - gasAfter == 6900 for oversized input (> 160 bytes)
Assert gasBefore - gasAfter == 6900 for empty input
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7951-INV-001. Covers ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-6900, STATE-GAS-CHARGED. Invariant type - attempting falsification through diverse input paths. If gas is not charged for invalid inputs, attacker can spam precompile calls cheaply.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-P2P-BLOCK-TO-FORKCHOICE: reject blocks at or before finalized slot
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a test node that has finalized at epoch E (slot S_fin = compute_start_slot_at_epoch(E)). 2. Craft a SignedBeaconBlock with slot == S_fin and a valid parent root. Send via P2P gossip. 3. Verify the block is REJECTED by on_block. 4. Craft a block with slot == S_fin - 1. Send via P2P. Verify REJECTED. 5. Craft a block with slot == S_fin + 1 with valid parent. Verify it proceeds past this check. 6. Check that the rejection fires before any state transition or DB writes occur.
executable_checks: Assert block with slot == finalized_slot is rejected with appropriate error
Assert block with slot < finalized_slot is rejected
Assert block with slot == finalized_slot + 1 passes this specific check
Assert no state mutation occurs for rejected blocks
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-PRECOND-003. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-P2P-BLOCK-TO-FORKCHOICE requires full validation pipeline. Attacker replays old finalized blocks via P2P. Accepting blocks at or before finalized slot could revert finality.

checklist.title: Verify finalized slot computation uses correct checkpoint epoch for boundary validation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify compute_start_slot_at_epoch(store.finalized_checkpoint.epoch) is used (not store.finalized_checkpoint.epoch directly). 2. Test at epoch boundaries: if finalized at epoch 10 (slot 320), verify slot 320 is rejected and slot 321 is accepted. 3. Test with non-zero SLOTS_PER_EPOCH offsets to ensure start-of-epoch computation is correct.
executable_checks: Assert finalized slot is computed as compute_start_slot_at_epoch(finalized_checkpoint.epoch)
Assert comparison is strictly greater-than (not >=)
Assert boundary is correct at epoch transitions
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-PRECOND-003. Supporting node check for ACTION-CHECK-AFTER-FINALIZED. Off-by-one in slot comparison or incorrect epoch-to-slot conversion could allow finalized-slot blocks.

checklist.title: Falsify validation completeness: attempt block acceptance with each individual assertion failing
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. For each validation check in on_block (parent known, slot ordering, finalized slot, finalized ancestry, data availability): craft a block that fails ONLY that specific check while passing all others. 2. Send each crafted block via P2P gossip. 3. Verify each block is rejected and does NOT enter the block store. 4. Specifically test: (a) unknown parent root, (b) slot <= parent slot, (c) slot <= finalized slot, (d) not descendant of finalized block, (e) missing data columns. 5. Verify no partial state is written on rejection.
executable_checks: Assert block with unknown parent_root is rejected
Assert block with slot <= parent.slot is rejected
Assert block failing finalized ancestry check is rejected
Assert block with missing data availability is rejected
Assert store.blocks does not contain any rejected block's root
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-FULUFC-INV-002. Invariant type - testing each rejection path independently. Critical: if any single assertion can be bypassed, invalid blocks corrupt fork choice for all nodes. Covers edges EDGE-PARENT-FAIL, EDGE-SLOT-FAIL, EDGE-FINALIZED-SLOT-FAIL, EDGE-ANCESTRY-FAIL, EDGE-DATA-FAIL.

checklist.title: Falsify RANDAO seed epoch selection for proposer lookahead computation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. In get_beacon_proposer_index or compute_proposer_index, verify the seed is retrieved via get_seed(state, epoch - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1, DOMAIN_BEACON_PROPOSER). 2. Compare the epoch parameter: it must be N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1 (where N is the target epoch), NOT N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD or N - 1. 3. Compute proposer schedules using both correct and incorrect seed epochs. 4. Verify that using epoch N - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD (off-by-one) produces different proposer assignments, confirming the seed epoch matters. 5. Verify the seed epoch predates any effective balance changes that could be manipulated.
executable_checks: Assert seed epoch == target_epoch - MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD - 1
Assert proposer schedule differs when using wrong seed epoch (off-by-one test)
Assert RANDAO mix at seed epoch was committed before effective balances for target epoch are known
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-INV-003. Invariant type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7917-01. Using wrong seed epoch weakens anti-grinding protection, allowing attackers to bias proposer selection via effective balance manipulation.

checklist.title: Falsify proposer_lookahead corruption detection and recovery behavior
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify that proposer_lookahead is recomputed deterministically from (effective_balances, RANDAO_seed) at each epoch boundary. 2. Corrupt the proposer_lookahead array in a test node's state (change one entry). 3. Verify the node detects the inconsistency on next block processing (proposer doesn't match expected). 4. Check what recovery action is taken: does the node resync, recompute, or continue with corrupt data? 5. If no recovery mechanism exists, confirm the node becomes unable to validate blocks correctly.
executable_checks: Assert proposer_lookahead is deterministic given same inputs
Assert corrupted lookahead causes block validation failures
Assert node behavior on corruption (resync vs crash vs silent failure)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7917-INV-006. Related ambiguity AMB-EIP7917-02. No explicit recovery procedure exists for corrupted lookahead. Corrupted lookahead requires full resync, taking affected nodes offline.

checklist.title: Falsify secp256r1 validation ordering: attempt to skip intermediate checks
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Test each validation step in isolation: (a) Input < 160 bytes → must return empty (no further checks). (b) Input = 160 bytes but r >= curve_order → must return empty. (c) Input with s >= curve_order → must return empty. (d) Input with public key not on secp256r1 curve → must return empty. (e) Input with point at infinity as public key → must return empty. 2. For each case, verify the precompile does NOT reach the signature verification step. 3. Craft a point NOT on secp256r1 (invalid curve) and verify it's rejected before ECDSA verify. 4. Test with r=0, s=0, r=curve_order, s=curve_order as boundary values.
executable_checks: Assert short input (< 160 bytes) returns empty without crash
Assert r >= secp256r1_order returns empty
Assert s >= secp256r1_order returns empty
Assert point not on curve returns empty before verification
Assert point at infinity returns empty
Assert r=0, s=0 boundary cases handled correctly
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W0-EIP7951-INV-006. Invariant type - testing validation ordering. Skipping curve membership check before verification could enable invalid curve attacks. Covers full validation pipeline: length → sig bounds → pubkey bounds → curve → infinity.

checklist.title: Falsify column mapping uniqueness: verify NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group produces no overlaps
checklist.bug_class: Data Availability Failure / Incorrect Column Assignment
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. For all valid custody_group values [0, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS) and all valid i values [0, columns_per_group): compute column_index = NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + custody_group. 2. Collect all column indices into a set. Verify set size equals total expected columns (NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS). 3. Verify no duplicates exist. 4. Verify all column indices are in range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS). 5. Test with actual Fulu config values: NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS=128, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS=128. 6. Verify each custody group maps to exactly the expected number of columns.
executable_checks: Assert all generated column indices are unique (set size == expected total)
Assert all column indices in [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS)
Assert each custody group maps to exactly NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS columns
Assert complete coverage: union of all custody group columns == all columns
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-INV-003. Invariant type. Critical: incorrect column mapping across all nodes would cause systematic data availability failures for the entire network.

checklist.title: Verify reconstructed column re-gossip is restricted to subscribed custody subnets
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a node with specific custody groups (e.g., groups [0, 1, 2]). 2. Trigger column reconstruction from received cells. 3. Monitor which pubsub topics the reconstructed columns are published to. 4. Verify columns are ONLY published to topics corresponding to the node's custody groups. 5. Verify columns belonging to non-custody groups are NOT re-gossiped.
executable_checks: Assert re-gossiped columns only go to custody group subnets
Assert no columns are published to non-custody subnets
Assert subnet computation matches compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-DASCORE-POSTCOND-006. Post-condition type. Re-gossiping on wrong subnets could cause network topology violations but receiving peers validate independently.

checklist.title: Falsify BPO fork timestamp ordering: verify BPO1 < BPO2 < BPO3 > Fusaka activation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Read all BPO fork timestamps from the chain config. 2. Verify strict ordering: FUSAKA_TIMESTAMP < BPO1_TIMESTAMP < BPO2_TIMESTAMP < BPO3_TIMESTAMP. 3. Test what happens if BPO timestamps are equal (BPO1 == BPO2): does the client handle this? 4. Test with reversed ordering and verify the client either rejects the config or handles it correctly. 5. Cross-check multiple client implementations for identical timestamp parsing.
executable_checks: Assert BPO1_TIMESTAMP > FUSAKA_TIMESTAMP
Assert BPO2_TIMESTAMP > BPO1_TIMESTAMP
Assert BPO3_TIMESTAMP > BPO2_TIMESTAMP
Assert client rejects or handles equal BPO timestamps
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7607-INV-002. Invariant type. Related ambiguity AMB-EIP7607-01. Misordered BPO activation could cause consensus split between nodes interpreting different blob parameters.

checklist.title: Falsify RLP block size limit enforcement during block construction
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Construct a block that is close to MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (fill with large transactions). 2. Verify the block builder checks RLP-encoded size before finalizing. 3. Attempt to add one more transaction that would push the block over MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE. 4. Verify the builder stops adding transactions. 5. Verify the final RLP-encoded block size is <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE. 6. Check if the size estimation accounts for RLP encoding overhead correctly.
executable_checks: Assert final RLP block size <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE
Assert block builder refuses transactions that would exceed limit
Assert RLP encoding overhead is accounted for in size estimation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP7934-PRECOND-002. Pre-condition type. Only affects the individual validator; network rejects oversized blocks correctly. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7934-03.

checklist.title: Falsify multi-provider requirement: attempt cell requests with single provider
checklist.bug_class: Single Point of Failure / Selective Withholding
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a sampler node. 2. Have only 1 peer announce as a provider for a specific blob. 3. Verify the sampler waits and does NOT request cells until at least 2 distinct providers are observed. 4. Add a second provider. Verify the sampler proceeds. 5. Test edge case: 2 announcements from same peer (should count as 1 provider). 6. Verify timeout behavior if second provider never appears.
executable_checks: Assert sampler blocks cell requests until >= 2 distinct providers observed
Assert duplicate announcements from same peer count as 1 provider
Assert sampler proceeds once 2 distinct providers announce
Assert timeout mechanism exists for insufficient providers
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-PRECOND-005. Pre-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP8070-03. Single-provider requests enable undetectable selective withholding.

checklist.title: Assess completeness of selective withholding and eclipse attack mitigations (TBD in spec)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Review spec sections marked TBD for selective withholding mitigations. 2. Check if noise column monitoring is implemented in clients. 3. Test: an attacker withholds specific columns from a sampler while providing others. 4. Verify whether the sampler detects the selective withholding pattern. 5. Check if peer scoring penalizes inconsistent providers. 6. Document gaps between spec TBD sections and current implementations.
executable_checks: Document which TBD threat mitigations are implemented vs missing
Test noise column monitoring if implemented
Verify peer scoring for selective withholding patterns
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W1-EIP8070-INV-005. Invariant type (informational). Related ambiguity AMB-EIP8070-03. Spec explicitly marks these threat models as TBD. Would need concrete exploit for higher severity.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-P2P-ETH69-BLOCKRANGEUPDATE: validate BlockRangeUpdate from untrusted peers
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a BlockRangeUpdate with earliestBlock > latestBlock. Verify peer rejects or ignores. 2. Send with latestBlock = MAX_UINT64. Verify no integer overflow in range computation. 3. Send with both = 0. Verify handled gracefully. 4. Send at rate exceeding once per epoch. Verify rate limiting. 5. Send valid range, then request blocks in that range from the peer - if peer can't serve, verify peer scoring penalty. 6. Test malformed RLP encoding of the message.
executable_checks: Assert earliestBlock > latestBlock is rejected
Assert MAX_UINT64 values don't cause overflow
Assert rate limiting prevents > 1 update per epoch per peer
Assert malformed RLP is handled without crash
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-HISTORY-PRECOND-01. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-P2P-ETH69-BLOCKRANGEUPDATE: BlockRangeUpdate messages must be rate-limited, false ranges must be penalized.

checklist.title: Verify peer selection logic handles extreme BlockRangeUpdate values safely
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. A peer claims range [0, 10^18]. Verify this does not cause excessive memory allocation in peer tracking data structures. 2. Multiple peers claim overlapping extreme ranges. Verify peer selection logic handles this without O(n^2) or worse complexity. 3. Verify that range sizes stored internally use bounded representations.
executable_checks: Assert memory usage bounded regardless of claimed range size
Assert peer selection algorithm is O(n) or better in number of peers
Assert claimed ranges stored in bounded data structures
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-HISTORY-PRECOND-01. Supporting node check. Extreme range claims could trigger resource exhaustion in peer selection.

checklist.title: Verify bloom filter recomputation from logs matches eth/68 format exactly
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Take a set of known receipts with their eth/68-format bloom filters. 2. Strip the bloom fields. Recompute blooms from the log entries. 3. Compare byte-for-byte: recomputed bloom must equal original. 4. Test with receipts containing 0 logs, 1 log, many logs. 5. Test with logs containing topics of various lengths. 6. Verify Keccak-256 hash function and bit-setting logic match the EIP-2 bloom filter specification exactly.
executable_checks: Assert recomputed bloom == original bloom for all test receipts
Assert bloom is correct for 0-log receipts (all zeros)
Assert bloom bit-setting follows EIP-2 specification exactly
Assert determinism: same logs always produce same bloom
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-EIP7642-RECEIPT-POSTCOND-01. Post-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7642-03. Incorrect bloom recomputation could cause receipt query failures affecting dApps.

checklist.title: Falsify parent validity check for data_column_sidecar gossip acceptance
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Create a valid data_column_sidecar whose parent_root references a block known to be invalid. 2. Submit via gossip. Verify the sidecar is REJECTED. 3. Test with parent_root referencing: (a) non-existent block, (b) block that was initially accepted but later invalidated, (c) block on a different fork. 4. Verify the rejection happens before any storage or forwarding.
executable_checks: Assert sidecar with invalid parent is REJECTED
Assert sidecar with unknown parent is not accepted (IGNORED or REJECTED)
Assert rejected sidecar is not forwarded to peers
Assert no storage of sidecar data for invalid parents
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-GOSSIP-PRECOND-07. Pre-condition type. Defense in depth: prevents propagation of data built on invalid chains.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-REQRESP-DATA-COLUMNS-BY-RANGE: enforce serve range limits
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute expected data_column_serve_range = [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH), current_epoch]. 2. Request columns for a slot BEFORE the serve range. Verify ResourceUnavailable (error 3). 3. Request columns for a slot AFTER current epoch. Verify rejection. 4. Request columns at exact boundary of serve range. Verify correct serving. 5. Request with count exceeding MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. Verify truncation or rejection. 6. Test immediately after FULU_FORK_EPOCH when serve range is minimal.
executable_checks: Assert requests before serve range return ResourceUnavailable
Assert requests after current epoch return error
Assert boundary slots are served correctly
Assert count > MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS is handled
Assert serve range correctly uses max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-REQRESP-PRECOND-02. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-REQRESP-DATA-COLUMNS-BY-RANGE: range must be checked, response limited, ordering enforced.

checklist.title: Verify serve range computation handles edge cases at FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. At epoch = FULU_FORK_EPOCH + 1: verify serve_range starts at FULU_FORK_EPOCH (not 0 or negative). 2. At epoch >> FULU_FORK_EPOCH: verify serve_range starts at current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. 3. At epoch = FULU_FORK_EPOCH: verify serve_range is [FULU_FORK_EPOCH, FULU_FORK_EPOCH]. 4. Test underflow: if current_epoch < MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, the max() clamp must prevent negative epochs.
executable_checks: Assert serve range floor = max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH)
Assert no integer underflow when current_epoch < MIN_EPOCHS
Assert serve range at FULU_FORK_EPOCH is valid
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-REQRESP-PRECOND-02. Supporting node check for serve range computation. Integer underflow risk when current_epoch < MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.

checklist.title: Verify anti-equivocation cache is updated for locally-imported columns (not just gossip)
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Have a proposer create a block with blobs. 2. Import the data columns via the local EL path (engine_getBlobsV2). 3. Check if the anti-equivocation cache now contains (slot, proposer_index, column_index) for each imported column. 4. Attempt to import a DIFFERENT set of columns for the same (slot, proposer_index) via gossip. 5. Verify the second import is detected as equivocation and REJECTED. 6. If the cache was NOT updated in step 3, the conflicting columns would be accepted, causing a consensus split.
executable_checks: Assert cache contains entries after local EL import
Assert conflicting columns for same (slot, proposer) detected as equivocation
Assert equivocation detection works identically for gossip and local paths
Assert cache entries match (slot, proposer_index, column_index) tuple format
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-BLOB-PUB-POSTCOND-01. Post-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-FULU-P2P-05. Critical: equivocation detection must work for all import paths, not just gossip. Cache miss on local path enables consensus splits.

checklist.title: Falsify peer quality invariant: verify ongoing compliance checking for connected peers
checklist.bug_class: Peer Quality Degradation / Network Efficiency Loss
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Connect to a peer that initially meets all requirements (fork compatibility, custody_group_count >= CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, responsive). 2. Have the peer stop responding to custody requests. 3. Verify the node detects this via ongoing scoring and eventually disconnects. 4. Have a peer change its ENR to advertise lower custody_group_count. Verify detection. 5. Verify that fork compatibility is rechecked at fork boundaries.
executable_checks: Assert unresponsive peers are eventually disconnected
Assert peers with insufficient custody count are scored down
Assert fork compatibility is maintained throughout connection
Assert peer scoring reflects actual custody behavior
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W2-FULU-DISCOVERY-INV-01. Invariant type. Maintaining peer quality throughout connection lifetime ensures data availability and network health.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-EL-PAYLOAD-VERIFICATION: EL verification required before block acceptance
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Send a block via P2P with a syntactically valid but semantically invalid execution payload (e.g., invalid state root, invalid transactions). 2. Verify the CL calls Engine API newPayload before accepting the block. 3. Mock the Engine API to return INVALID. Verify the CL rejects the block. 4. Test what happens if Engine API times out: does CL accept the block or wait? 5. Verify CL validates execution payload structure (blob_kzg_commitments count vs get_blob_parameters) independently of EL. 6. Test with Engine API returning SYNCING: verify block is not prematurely accepted.
executable_checks: Assert CL calls newPayload before block acceptance
Assert INVALID response causes block rejection
Assert SYNCING response does not cause premature acceptance
Assert timeout does not cause silent acceptance
Assert CL independently validates blob commitment count
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-EXEC-PAYLOAD-PRE-002. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-EL-PAYLOAD-VERIFICATION: CL must validate independently before trusting EL result. Skipping EL verification would allow invalid state transitions.

checklist.title: Verify CL pre-validates execution payload fields before Engine API call
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify CL checks blob_kzg_commitments length against get_blob_parameters(epoch) before calling Engine API. 2. Send a block with blob_kzg_commitments count exceeding the per-block limit. Verify CL rejects without calling EL. 3. Verify execution payload header fields (parent_hash, block_number, etc.) are structurally validated by CL.
executable_checks: Assert blob commitment count validated before Engine API call
Assert excess commitments rejected at CL level
Assert structural validation of execution payload fields
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-EXEC-PAYLOAD-PRE-002. Supporting node check. CL should filter obviously invalid payloads before making Engine API calls.

checklist.title: Falsify reserve price condition: test for integer overflow in BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee multiplication
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute BLOB_BASE_COST (2^13 = 8192) * base_fee_per_gas for extreme base_fee values. 2. Test with base_fee = 2^245 (maximum realistic): verify 2^13 * 2^245 = 2^258 doesn't overflow uint256. 3. Compare against GAS_PER_BLOB * get_blob_basefee(parent): test same extreme values. 4. Verify the comparison uses the correct operator: > (not >=). 5. Cross-check: implement the condition in multiple languages (Python, Go, Rust) and verify identical results for edge cases. 6. Related ambiguity AMB-EIP7918-01: verify the mode selection is correct.
executable_checks: Assert no uint256 overflow for max realistic base_fee values
Assert comparison operator is strictly greater-than
Assert mode selection matches spec for boundary values
Assert identical results across Python reference and client implementations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-PRE-001. Pre-condition type. Related ambiguity AMB-EIP7918-01. BLOB_BASE_COST * base_fee multiplication could overflow in some implementations. Wrong mode selection affects all blocks.

checklist.title: Falsify cross-client consensus: verify identical excess_blob_gas computation across implementations
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Generate a comprehensive test vector set covering: (a) reserve mode transitions, (b) normal mode transitions, (c) boundary between modes, (d) zero blob_gas_used, (e) max blob_gas_used, (f) values near integer division boundaries. 2. Run test vectors through all client implementations (geth, nethermind, besu, erigon, reth). 3. Compare excess_blob_gas output for every test case. 4. Pay special attention to integer division rounding: Python // vs Go / vs Rust / behavior. 5. Test the reserve calculation formula: parent.excess_blob_gas + parent.blob_gas_used * BLOB_BASE_COST // parent.base_fee_per_gas.
executable_checks: Assert all clients produce identical excess_blob_gas for same inputs
Assert integer division rounding is consistent across implementations
Assert reserve and normal mode formulas match spec exactly
Assert mode selection boundary produces consistent results
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-RESERVE-INV-004. Invariant type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7918-02. Implementation divergence in consensus-critical calculations splits the network along client boundaries.

checklist.title: Falsify monotonicity of excess_blob_gas in reserve mode
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Simulate a sequence of blocks in reserve mode with varying blob_gas_used values. 2. For each block, verify excess_blob_gas[n+1] >= excess_blob_gas[n] (monotonically non-decreasing). 3. Test edge case: blob_gas_used = 0 in reserve mode. The formula should still add (since it only adds in reserve mode). 4. Test transition from reserve to normal mode: verify excess_blob_gas may now decrease. 5. Verify the formula: excess = parent.excess + parent.blob_gas_used * BLOB_BASE_COST / parent.base_fee always produces non-negative addition.
executable_checks: Assert excess_blob_gas never decreases in reserve mode across block sequences
Assert excess_blob_gas may decrease in normal mode when blob_gas_used < target
Assert formula correctness for blob_gas_used = 0 in reserve mode
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-EIP7918-EXCESS-INV-002. Invariant type. Violations of monotonicity in reserve mode indicate implementation bugs that would cause consensus divergence.

checklist.title: Verify complete Fulu fork activation with all new state fields initialized
checklist.bug_class: Incomplete Fork Activation / State Initialization Failure
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process blocks up to the Fulu fork epoch. 2. After the fork transition, verify: (a) state.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION, (b) state.fork.previous_version == ELECTRA_FORK_VERSION, (c) state.fork.epoch == FULU_FORK_EPOCH, (d) state.proposer_lookahead is initialized and non-empty. 3. Verify that the first block after fork uses Fulu processing rules (not Electra). 4. Test: process a block that is only valid under Fulu rules (e.g., with new blob limits). Verify acceptance. 5. Process a block that would only be valid under pre-Fulu rules. Verify rejection.
executable_checks: Assert fork version fields correct after transition
Assert proposer_lookahead initialized and populated
Assert Fulu processing rules active for first post-fork block
Assert pre-Fulu-only valid blocks rejected post-fork
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W3-FULU-FORK-TRANSITION-POST-003. Post-condition type. Incomplete fork activation would cause all blocks after the fork to be processed incorrectly, affecting all nodes.

checklist.title: Falsify BPO parameter irreversibility: test chain reorg across fork boundary
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process blocks past a BPO fork activation point. Verify blob parameters are post-BPO values. 2. Trigger a chain reorg that goes back before the BPO activation. 3. Re-process the canonical chain. 4. Verify blob parameters are STILL post-BPO after reorg resolution (if the reorg target is after BPO). 5. If the reorg reverts to before BPO, verify parameters correctly revert only temporarily and re-activate when the chain catches up to BPO timestamp. 6. Verify no state corruption from the reorg.
executable_checks: Assert blob parameters remain post-BPO after reorg that stays after activation
Assert parameters correctly transition during reorg across boundary
Assert no state corruption from fork boundary reorg
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7892-INV-002. Invariant type. Parameter reversion after fork activation would cause consensus divergence on reorgs across the BPO fork boundary.

checklist.title: Verify ModExp computation correctness for edge cases and cross-client consistency
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Test edge cases: (a) modulus = 0 → result must be zero bytes of modulus_length, (b) exponent = 0 → result must be 1 mod modulus, (c) base = 0 → result must be 0, (d) base^exp where result > modulus (verify correct reduction). 2. Test with inputs at new EIP-7823 upper bounds (1024 bytes each). 3. Test with modulus_length = 0, base_length = 0, exp_length = 0. 4. Verify zero-padding: result must be exactly modulus_length bytes. 5. Cross-check results across all EL clients for identical outputs. 6. Test with inputs that previously caused known divergences.
executable_checks: Assert modulus=0 returns zero bytes of correct length
Assert exponent=0 returns 1 mod modulus
Assert base=0 returns 0
Assert result is zero-padded to modulus_length bytes
Assert identical results across client implementations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W4-EIP7883-POSTCOND-003. Post-condition type. Incorrect ModExp result causes state root divergence, splitting all nodes. Focus on edge cases.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-DISCOVERY-ENR-CUSTODY: prevent eclipse attacks on column peers
checklist.bug_class: Eclipse Attack / Sybil Attack on DA
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Set up a target node. Flood the discovery layer with Sybil nodes claiming custody of specific columns. 2. Monitor whether the target node's peer set becomes dominated by Sybil peers for those columns. 3. Verify the node enforces peer diversity (e.g., IP diversity, subnet diversity, ASN diversity). 4. Test if a node connects to multiple peers for the same custody group to avoid single-point-of-failure. 5. Verify ENR cgc (custody_group_count) is validated: reject peers with cgc < CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT. 6. Verify fork digest matching in ENR.
executable_checks: Assert peer diversity is enforced across custody groups
Assert ENR cgc >= CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT enforced
Assert ENR fork digest matching prevents cross-fork connections
Assert Sybil flood does not monopolize specific column peer sets
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-PRECOND-003. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-DISCOVERY-ENR-CUSTODY: ENR fields must be validated, cgc must meet requirements. Eclipse attack could cause false data unavailability conclusions.

checklist.title: Verify peer discovery ensures minimum peer count per custody group
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the node maintains a minimum number of peers per custody group it needs to sample. 2. If peers for a group drop below minimum, verify the node actively seeks new peers. 3. Test with gradual peer churn: verify the node adapts. 4. Verify sampling does not proceed if insufficient peers are available for required groups.
executable_checks: Assert minimum peer count maintained per custody group
Assert active peer discovery when count drops below minimum
Assert sampling waits for sufficient peers
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-PRECOND-003. Supporting node check for peer discovery. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7594-03.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for custody assignment: node ID manipulation resistance
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Analyze the custody group assignment formula: compute_custody_groups(node_id, custody_group_count). 2. Attempt to find node_id values that concentrate custody on specific target columns. 3. Calculate the computational cost of generating a node_id that custodies a specific set of columns. 4. Verify node_id is derived from a key that is expensive to generate (e.g., requires PoW or staking). 5. Test distribution: generate 10000 random node_ids and verify custody assignments are approximately uniform across groups.
executable_checks: Assert custody group distribution is approximately uniform for random node IDs
Assert computational cost of targeting specific groups is prohibitive
Assert node_id derivation includes anti-grinding measures
Assert no easily-discoverable node_id patterns for custody concentration
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-DAS-ASSUM-001. Boundary property (Invariant type). Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7594-02. Custody concentration attack could allow targeted data withholding affecting >33% of network's DA guarantees.

checklist.title: Falsify reconstruction threshold: attempt reconstruction with insufficient columns
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Collect exactly 49% of total columns for a blob. Attempt reconstruction. Verify it fails or is not attempted. 2. Collect exactly 50% of columns. Attempt reconstruction. Verify it succeeds. 3. Test with 50% - 1 column. Verify failure. 4. If a client attempts reconstruction below threshold, verify the output is flagged as invalid or the attempt is blocked. 5. Verify the threshold check uses NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS / 2 (not a different formula).
executable_checks: Assert reconstruction not attempted with < 50% columns
Assert reconstruction succeeds with exactly 50% columns
Assert threshold boundary (50% - 1) correctly prevents reconstruction
Assert reconstructed data matches original when threshold met
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7594-RECON-PRECOND-002. Pre-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7594-04. Premature reconstruction produces corrupted blob data, affecting nodes relying on reconstructed data.

checklist.title: Verify MODEXP consumes all gas and returns error when input exceeds 1024 bytes
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call MODEXP with base_length = 1025 (just over limit). Measure gas consumed. Verify ALL gas is consumed. 2. Repeat for exp_length = 1025, mod_length = 1025. 3. Verify the return value is empty/error (not a valid result). 4. Test boundary: exactly 1024 bytes → must succeed normally with standard gas cost. 5. Test with all three lengths at 1024 → must succeed. 6. Test with one at 1025 and others at 0 → must consume all gas. 7. Cross-check gas consumption behavior across all EL clients for IDENTICAL behavior.
executable_checks: Assert input with any length > 1024 consumes ALL provided gas
Assert input with all lengths <= 1024 executes normally
Assert return value is empty/error for over-limit inputs
Assert boundary 1024 works, 1025 fails
Assert identical gas behavior across all EL clients
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7823-VAL-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition type. Related ambiguity AMB-EIP7823-01. Different gas consumption across clients on violation causes consensus split, crashing the entire network.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for BOUNDARY-TX-GAS-LIMIT-MEMPOOL: reject transactions exceeding gas cap
checklist.bug_class: Gas Cap Bypass / Transaction Pool Pollution
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Submit a transaction with gasLimit = 16,777,217 (2^24 + 1) via P2P. Verify rejection. 2. Submit with gasLimit = 16,777,216 (exactly 2^24). Verify acceptance. 3. Submit with gasLimit = MAX_UINT64. Verify rejection. 4. Monitor: does the rejected transaction get propagated to any peer? It must NOT. 5. Submit via JSON-RPC (if possible): verify it's also rejected at mempool level. 6. Include an over-cap transaction in a block received via P2P. Verify the entire block is rejected.
executable_checks: Assert gasLimit = 2^24 + 1 is rejected at mempool
Assert gasLimit = 2^24 is accepted
Assert rejected transaction is NOT propagated to peers
Assert block containing over-cap transaction is rejected
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7825-TX-POSTCOND-001. Boundary property. Trust model edges BOUNDARY-TX-GAS-LIMIT-MEMPOOL and BOUNDARY-BLOCK-GAS-LIMIT-P2P: gasLimit checked at both mempool and block validation levels.

checklist.title: Verify gas cap enforcement in block validation rejects blocks with over-cap transactions
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Craft a valid-looking block where one transaction has gasLimit = 2^24 + 1. 2. Send via P2P. Verify entire block is rejected. 3. Test: what if the block was produced by a malicious validator who bypassed their own mempool checks? Verify receiving nodes still reject. 4. Verify the check is in the block validation path, not just mempool.
executable_checks: Assert block with over-cap transaction is rejected during block validation
Assert validation is independent of mempool (works for received blocks)
Assert rejection reason is clearly gas limit cap violation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W5-EIP7825-TX-POSTCOND-001. Supporting node check for block-level validation. Trust model edge BOUNDARY-BLOCK-GAS-LIMIT-P2P requires per-transaction gasLimit check in received blocks.

checklist.title: Falsify fork upgrade ordering: verify upgrade_to_fulu runs after epoch processing
checklist.bug_class: Fork Processing Order Violation / State Divergence
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process the fork epoch boundary. 2. Verify the execution order: (a) process slots up to fork epoch, (b) run normal epoch processing (justification, finalization, etc.), (c) THEN call upgrade_to_fulu. 3. Compare state roots: process with correct order vs reversed order. They must differ. 4. Verify all client implementations use the same ordering. 5. Related ambiguity AMB-FULU-FORK-02: confirm the spec is unambiguous on this ordering.
executable_checks: Assert epoch processing completes before upgrade_to_fulu is called
Assert state root differs between correct and incorrect ordering
Assert all clients implement same ordering
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-FORK-ST-PRECOND-003. Pre-condition type. Related ambiguity AMB-FULU-FORK-02. Wrong ordering of epoch processing vs fork upgrade produces different post-state, causing consensus split.

checklist.title: Verify DataColumnSidecar published to correct subnet via compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar
checklist.bug_class: Subnet Routing Error / Data Availability Degradation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. For each column_index in [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS), compute the subnet via compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(column_index). 2. Verify the formula: column_index % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT. 3. Publish a sidecar for column_index = 5. Verify it goes to subnet 5 % SUBNET_COUNT. 4. Monitor the actual pubsub topic used. Verify it matches data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id}. 5. Test all column indices to ensure coverage of all subnets.
executable_checks: Assert subnet = column_index % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT for all columns
Assert published topic matches expected subnet
Assert all subnets receive approximately equal column distribution
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-FULU-VAL-SIDECAR-POSTCOND-002. Post-condition type. Wrong subnet mapping causes data column unavailability, affecting sampling for >5% of the network if the bug is in a popular client.

checklist.title: Falsify history expiry precondition: verify EIP-7642 and deposit log processing gates
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the client checks that eth/69 (EIP-7642) protocol is fully active before allowing history expiry. 2. Verify the client checks that all pre-merge deposit logs have been migrated to CL via EIP-6110. 3. Attempt to trigger history expiry before these conditions are met. Verify it's blocked. 4. Test: what happens if a client drops pre-merge history while deposit logs haven't been processed? Verify the CL can still access all historical deposits. 5. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7927-03.
executable_checks: Assert history expiry blocked when EIP-7642 not implemented
Assert history expiry blocked when deposit logs not fully processed
Assert both gates must be satisfied for expiry to proceed
Assert CL deposit access maintained after proper expiry
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-EIP7927-PRECOND-001. Pre-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7927-03. Premature history expiry before deposit log processing could cause CL to miss validator deposits, affecting validator activation for >33% of the network.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-PROPOSER-SELECTED: reject blocks from non-assigned proposers
checklist.bug_class: Unauthorized Block Injection / Fork Choice Manipulation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute the proposer_lookahead for the current epoch. 2. Have a validator NOT assigned to slot S create a signed block for slot S. 3. Send via P2P gossip. Verify the block is REJECTED because proposer_index doesn't match lookahead[S]. 4. Verify the check uses the deterministic proposer_lookahead array (EIP-7917), not a recomputed value. 5. Test with a valid signature from the wrong proposer: the signature must be valid for the proposer's key, but the proposer must not be assigned to the slot. 6. Verify this check occurs before state transition.
executable_checks: Assert block from non-assigned proposer is rejected
Assert proposer verification uses deterministic lookahead array
Assert valid signature from wrong proposer still rejected
Assert check occurs before any state transition
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-BOUNDARY-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-001. Boundary property. Trust model edge: proposer must match lookahead. Related assumption ASSUM-FULU-FORK-02. Accepting unauthorized blocks could cause fork choice manipulation affecting >33% of network.

checklist.title: Verify proposer_lookahead consistency between block proposer check and epoch computation
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Compute proposer_lookahead at epoch N. 2. At each slot in epoch N, verify the block proposer check reads from the same lookahead array. 3. Ensure no race condition: lookahead cannot be updated mid-epoch. 4. Verify lookahead is stored in BeaconState and transitions atomically.
executable_checks: Assert lookahead immutable within an epoch once computed
Assert block proposer check reads from stored lookahead
Assert no race between epoch processing and block validation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W6-BOUNDARY-MALICIOUS-VALIDATOR-001. Supporting node check. Lookahead must be consistent between computation and usage to prevent time-of-check-time-of-use issues.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-BLOCK-GOSSIP-CL: reject oversized blocks at gossip layer
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Craft a beacon block that exceeds 10 MiB in serialized (SSZ) form. 2. Send via gossip. Verify the receiving node rejects it before full deserialization. 3. Verify the check is at the gossip layer (libp2p message size), not at block processing. 4. Test exactly at 10 MiB boundary: 10 MiB should pass, 10 MiB + 1 byte should fail. 5. Verify rejected oversized messages are NOT forwarded. 6. Verify the 10 MiB limit accounts for SSZ encoding, not just payload.
executable_checks: Assert block > 10 MiB is rejected at gossip layer
Assert block <= 10 MiB is accepted for further processing
Assert rejection happens before full deserialization
Assert rejected messages not forwarded to peers
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7935-SECBND-POSTCOND-001. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-BLOCK-GOSSIP-CL: block size validated against 10 MiB limit. Failure enables gossip network flooding.

checklist.title: Verify CL gossip size limit correctly accounts for EIP-7934 RLP block size interactions
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the CL gossip limit (10 MiB) is consistent with the EL MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE limit. 2. Construct a block at the EL RLP size limit. Verify its SSZ-wrapped CL representation is within the 10 MiB gossip limit. 3. If the EL limit allows blocks that exceed the CL gossip limit after SSZ wrapping, this is a split risk. 4. Verify both limits account for all encoding overhead.
executable_checks: Assert EL max RLP block fits within CL 10 MiB gossip limit after wrapping
Assert no block can be EL-valid but CL-gossip-rejected due to size
Assert encoding overhead is accounted for in limit calculations
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7935-SECBND-POSTCOND-001. Supporting node check. Size limit coordination between EL (EIP-7934 RLP limit) and CL (10 MiB gossip limit) must be consistent.

checklist.title: Verify compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs produces exactly CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells and proofs
checklist.bug_class: Cell Count Mismatch / PeerDAS Distribution Failure
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Call compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs with a valid blob. 2. Count the returned cells. Assert count == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. 3. Count the returned proofs. Assert count == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. 4. Test with various blob contents: all zeros, all ones, random, maximum field elements. 5. Verify cell indices are [0, CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB). 6. Test with a blob of all zero bytes (valid) and verify output shape.
executable_checks: Assert len(cells) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB
Assert len(proofs) == CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB
Assert each cell has correct byte length (BYTES_PER_CELL)
Assert each proof has correct byte length (BYTES_PER_PROOF)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-ENCODE-POSTCOND-002. Post-condition type. Wrong cell count would cause all peers requesting specific cell indices to fail verification, potentially affecting >33% of the network.

checklist.title: Verify KZG batch pairing check rejects cells with incorrect polynomial evaluations
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Generate valid cells and proofs via compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs. Verify batch verification passes. 2. Modify one byte in one cell. Verify batch verification now FAILS. 3. Replace one proof with a random valid G1 point. Verify FAILS. 4. Submit a batch where one cell's data doesn't match its commitment. Verify FAILS. 5. Test the random linear combination: modify cells in a way that might cancel out in the linear combination. Verify still FAILS. 6. Test batch of size 1 and batch of maximum size.
executable_checks: Assert valid cells+proofs pass batch verification
Assert single-byte modification in any cell causes failure
Assert wrong proof causes failure
Assert mismatched commitment causes failure
Assert batch verification with manipulated linear combination fails
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-VERIFY-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-PCS-FULU-02. Broken pairing verification completely undermines data availability.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for EDGE-CELL-VERIFY-P2P: BLS subgroup checks on deserialization
checklist.bug_class: Cryptographic Soundness Break / Missing Subgroup Check
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Craft a 48-byte value that represents a point on the BLS12-381 curve but NOT in the prime-order G1 subgroup (cofactor group point). 2. Submit as a KZG commitment in a data column sidecar via P2P. 3. Verify the deserialization function (bytes_to_kzg_commitment) REJECTS this input. 4. Similarly test bytes_to_kzg_proof with a cofactor point. 5. If the subgroup check is missing, construct a PoC where invalid data passes the pairing check due to the cofactor component. 6. Verify that the point-at-infinity (valid G1 point) is handled correctly.
executable_checks: Assert cofactor group point rejected by bytes_to_kzg_commitment
Assert cofactor group point rejected by bytes_to_kzg_proof
Assert valid G1 subgroup points accepted
Assert point-at-infinity handled correctly
Assert random 48-byte strings rejected (not on curve)
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-SECBND-PRECOND-003. Boundary property. Trust model edge EDGE-CELL-VERIFY-P2P: all inputs must be fully validated including subgroup checks. Missing subgroup checks break KZG proof soundness, allowing invalid data to be accepted as available by all nodes.

checklist.title: Verify complete input validation chain for P2P cell/proof exchange
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Verify the full validation chain per trust model: (a) byte length checks for commitments (BYTES_PER_COMMITMENT = 48), proofs (BYTES_PER_PROOF = 48), cells (BYTES_PER_CELL). (b) cell index bounds < CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB. (c) BLS G1 subgroup checks. (d) field element range < BLS_MODULUS. (e) KZG proof verification. 2. For each validation step, craft an input that fails ONLY that step. 3. Verify each failing input is rejected. 4. Verify the order of checks (cheapest first for DoS resistance).
executable_checks: Assert wrong-length commitment (47 or 49 bytes) rejected
Assert cell_index >= CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB rejected
Assert field element >= BLS_MODULUS rejected
Assert each validation step independently rejects invalid input
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-PCS-SECBND-PRECOND-003. Supporting node check. Complete validation chain must be enforced in order. Any gap allows invalid data through the boundary.

checklist.title: Verify all 4 Prague EL EIPs activate simultaneously at fork timestamp
checklist.detection_procedure: 1. Process blocks up to the Prague fork timestamp. 2. At the first post-Prague block, verify all 4 EIPs are active: (a) EIP-2537 (BLS precompile): call the BLS12-381 precompile, verify it works. (b) EIP-2935 (BLOCKHASH): verify the system contract is deployed and functional. (c) EIP-7623 (calldata cost increase): verify increased calldata cost applies. (d) EIP-7702 (delegation): verify SetCode transactions are accepted. 3. Verify that pre-Prague none of these are active. 4. Cross-check: ensure no client activates these EIPs at different blocks.
executable_checks: Assert BLS precompile active at first post-Prague block
Assert BLOCKHASH system contract active at first post-Prague block
Assert increased calldata cost at first post-Prague block
Assert SetCode transactions accepted at first post-Prague block
Assert none active at last pre-Prague block
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-W7-EIP7600-EL-POSTCOND-001. Post-condition type. Related assumption ASSUM-EIP7600-01. Partial EIP activation in some clients causes consensus disagreements affecting >33% of the network.
